narratives.Description: ci: scope the OVPR fixture jobs to launcher/hook changes; Windows leg off pull requests
narratives.Overview:
1. Path script (P1, P3, P4). A new script `.github/scripts/ovpr-fixture-paths.mjs` reads a newline list of changed paths and prints `ovpr_paths=true` when any path matches the list in item 2, else `ovpr_paths=false`. It exports its matcher so a test can call it.
2. Path list (P1, P3, P4): `packages/cli/**` (launcher and `deft-hook`), `packages/runtime/**`, `packages/content/**`, `packages/types/**`, `packages/core/package.json`, `packages/core/src/hooks/**`, `packages/core/src/deposit/**`, `packages/core/src/init-deposit/**`, `packages/core/src/install-contract/**`, `packages/core/src/install-health/**`, `packages/core/src/release-e2e/**`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/scripts/ovpr-fixture-paths.mjs`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `.nvmrc`.
3. `changes` job wiring (P1). A new step and an output `ovpr_paths` on the `changes` job. It runs only on `pull_request`. It lists files with `git diff --name-only --no-renames` between the merge base and the PR head (as `compute-artifact-only.sh` does), loads the script from the base tree with `git show "${BASE}:<script>"` (as the artifact-only predicate does), and passes branch names and SHAs through quoted environment variables. If the base is unusable, the script is absent on the base, or the diff fails, it writes `ovpr_paths=true`. It writes `false` only after a successful diff and match.
4. ubuntu fixture (P1, P3, P4). `ovpr-fixture` gets `if: always() && needs.changes.outputs.artifact_only != 'true' && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.changes.outputs.ovpr_paths != 'false')`. A missing or empty output runs the job. Push and merge_group behaviour is unchanged.
5. Windows fixture (P2, P3). `ovpr-fixture-windows` gets `if: always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.changes.outputs.artifact_only != 'true'`. The workflow's push trigger is master only, so it runs on master pushes and not on pull requests or merge_group. Its header comment says it moves to pull requests or required only at the Phase 4 exit.
6. Tests (P1-P4). In `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/ci_lifecycle_lane.test.ts`: the `changes` job exposes `ovpr_paths`; both `if:` conditions are as in items 4 and 5; the matcher returns false for a docs-only list and a scope-code list (`packages/core/src/scope/...`), and true for a launcher file (`packages/cli/src/launcher.ts`), a hook file (`packages/core/src/hooks/...`) and a content-staging file (`packages/content/stage-pack.mjs`); the wiring writes `true` when the script is absent on the base or the base is unusable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the `changes` job exposes an `ovpr_paths` output computed on pull requests from the merge-base diff by `.github/scripts/ovpr-fixture-paths.mjs` loaded from the base tree, and writes `true` when the base is unusable, the script is absent on the base, or the diff fails.
- In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `ovpr-fixture` runs on a pull request unless `ovpr_paths` is exactly `false`, and still runs on push and merge_group when the change is not artifact-only.
- In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `ovpr-fixture-windows` runs only on push events (master), not on pull requests or merge_group.
- In `.github/scripts/ovpr-fixture-paths.mjs`, the path list covers the launcher, runtime, content and types packages, `packages/core/package.json`, the core hook, deposit, init-deposit, install-contract, install-health and release-e2e folders, `ci.yml`, the script itself, and the root toolchain files.
- In `ci_lifecycle_lane.test.ts`, tests show a docs-only and a scope-code change set give `ovpr_paths=false`, a launcher, hook or content-staging change set gives `true`, and both job conditions are pinned.

- Workflow-level `paths:` filters (Stop 1 constraint).

issueCommentThread.body:
## Timing evidence

Sample: 123 `ci.yml` runs created after 2026-11-18T20:40Z, about 11 hours (65 pull_request, 32 merge_group, 26 push). Measured read-only through the REST API.

| Job | Runs | Median | p90 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OVPR lifecycle fixture (ubuntu) | 123 | 1.5 min | 1.7 min | 176 min |
| OVPR lifecycle fixture (Windows) | 122 | 6.3 min | 8.0 min | 780 min |

- Both fixture jobs together: 957 of 5,270 job-minutes (18.1%).
- Billed, with Windows at 2x: 1,736 of 6,556 minutes (26.5%).
- The Windows fixture uses 780 of 1,286 Windows minutes (60.7%).
- 26 of the 65 PR runs were on PRs that touched no launcher, runtime, hook, deposit or install path. They used 199 fixture minutes. A path filter would have skipped these.
- Wall-clock: the Windows fixture finished last in 16 of 122 runs and added about 1.1 min on average (3 min at most). The ubuntu job never finished last.
- Release path: no impact. The jobs exist only in `ci.yml`, which does not run on tags. `release.yml` and `npm-publish.yml` do not call the fixture CLI.

The main cost is runner minutes, not wall-clock. The Windows leg on pull_request and merge_group is most of it.

## In plain English
The two OVPR lifecycle fixture jobs in `ci.yml` run on every pull request that is not artifact-only. Each does a full install and build, and the Windows leg is the expensive one. The recommended fix adds one path output to the existing `changes` job, runs the ubuntu fixture on a pull request only when that output says launcher, runtime, hook, deposit or install files changed, and runs the Windows leg on master pushes only. Neither job is in the merge gate's `needs`, so required checks do not change.

Pain source: the four pains are the issue's `## Acceptance Criteria` items as written. The timing comment (7013657343) is evidence for the cost, not extra criteria.

## Pains
- P1 — On pull requests, the OVPR fixture jobs run only when the change set touches launcher, runtime, hook, deposit or install files, through a path filter on the existing `changes` job outputs.
- P2 — The Windows fixture leg runs on pushes to master (or a schedule), not on every pull request, until the Phase 4 exit makes it required.
- P3 — A pull request that changes only unrelated files (for example docs or scope code) runs neither fixture job.
- P4 — A pull request that changes a launcher or hook file still runs the fixture job.

## Excluded (not pains, not in this arc)
- Making either fixture job required, or adding it to the merge gate's `needs` (the Phase 4 exit, a separate reviewed change).
- Other CI cost work (#6584, #6585, #6586), the `artifact_only` allowlist, and the queue-reuse lookup.
- Ownership: the jobs were added by polfer in #6698 (installer/OVPR area). The operator relays polfer's approval to take this issue through to merge, limited to its four criteria.

## Constraints (not pains)
- No workflow-level `paths:` or `paths-ignore:` (ci_lifecycle_lane.test.ts 145-150 pins this; the required aggregators must still report).
- No new gate, grant or policy flag. Required check names and the merge gate's `needs` do not change.
- Fail-open for the fixture: when the path output cannot be computed (no usable base, unknown event), the ubuntu fixture runs.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` 3-10 (`on:` pull_request, push to master, merge_group).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` 91-175: the `changes` job. Outputs 94-98 (`artifact_only`, `queue_passed`, `queue_run_id`, `queue_run_attempt`); the predicate step 104-148 fetches the base and diffs against it with `fetch-depth: 0`; merge_group routes to the full stack at 119-123; `.github/scripts/compute-artifact-only.sh` 44 lists files with `git diff --name-only --no-renames --diff-filter=ACDMRT "${BASE}...${TIP}"`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` 1117-1157: `ovpr-fixture` (ubuntu, `if: always() && needs.changes.outputs.artifact_only != 'true'` at 1125, 12 min cap).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` 1159-1191: `ovpr-fixture-windows` (windows-latest, same `if:` at 1165, 15 min cap, step 4 only).
- `packages/core/src/release-e2e/packed-consumer.ts` 88-115: the fixture packs the launcher (`packages/cli`, `@deftai/directive`) and the runtime (`packages/runtime`, `@deftai/directive-runtime`) and installs both; `ovpr-lifecycle-fixture.ts` runs each host's registered hook command.
- Tests that read ci.yml job blocks: `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/ci_lifecycle_lane.test.ts` (145-150 no workflow-level paths; 179-196 non-required jobs gate on `artifact_only`), `ci_queue_reuse.test.ts` 151-191, `merge_queue_6295.test.ts` 36-50. None names the fixture jobs today.

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- R1 (P1). Add a step and an output `ovpr_paths` to the `changes` job. On `pull_request` it lists the changed files against the merge base (`git diff --name-only --no-renames origin/<base>...<head>`, as the predicate does) and writes `ovpr_paths=true` when any path matches the list in R2, else `false`. On any other event, or when the base is unusable, it writes `true`.
- R2 (P1, P3, P4). The path list: `packages/cli/**` (launcher and `deft-hook`), `packages/runtime/**` (runtime, staging and pack scripts), `packages/core/src/hooks/**` (hook), `packages/core/src/deposit/**` and `packages/core/src/init-deposit/**` (deposit), `packages/core/src/install-contract/**` and `packages/core/src/install-health/**` (install), `packages/core/src/release-e2e/**` (the fixture itself), `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `.nvmrc` (toolchain and dependencies).
- R3 (P1, P3, P4). `ovpr-fixture` gets `if: always() && needs.changes.outputs.artifact_only != 'true' && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.changes.outputs.ovpr_paths == 'true')`. Push and merge_group behaviour is unchanged.
- R4 (P2, P3). `ovpr-fixture-windows` gets `if: always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.changes.outputs.artifact_only != 'true'`, so it runs on master pushes only (the workflow's push trigger is master only). Its header comment says why and names the Phase 4 exit.
- R5 (P1-P4). A test in `ci_lifecycle_lane.test.ts` pins the `ovpr_paths` output, both `if:` conditions and the path list, and runs the path-match logic on a docs-only list, a scope-code list (`packages/core/src/scope/...`) and a launcher or hook list.

Questions for the critic:
1. Is the R2 path list right for "launcher, runtime, hook, deposit or install files"? The runtime bundle stages all of `packages/core`, so a change elsewhere in core can still break the fixture; is a named list the right trade, or should the list be broader?
2. Should the path logic live inline in the `changes` job, or in a script under `.github/scripts/` read from the base tree like the artifact-only predicate? The fixture jobs are advisory, and HEAD's workflow already decides their conditions on a pull request.
3. Is master push enough for the Windows leg, given that with queue reuse (#6584) a push can skip other jobs, or should it also run on a schedule?
4. Should the ubuntu fixture keep running on merge_group, or follow the path filter there too?

## In plain English

These advisory fixtures spend runner time on changes that do not need immediate lifecycle feedback, especially on Windows. The proposed event split is sensible, but the Ubuntu condition needs correction: it currently skips the fixture when the path output is missing, contrary to the stated fallback.

My answers to the four questions:

1. Keep a named path list rather than all core code, but include the direct packaging inputs missing from R2. Describe it as selective PR coverage, not a complete dependency boundary.
2. Prefer a small script read from the base tree, following the existing predicate mechanism. Include that script’s path in the trigger list. This permits behavioral tests and preserves the existing trust boundary.
3. Master pushes are sufficient for the proposed advisory Windows coverage. R4 does not consult `queue_passed`, so queue reuse does not suppress it. A schedule is unnecessary for this scope.
4. Keep Ubuntu running on merge groups. That retains integrated lifecycle coverage for changes deliberately excluded from PR filtering.

Verification used pinned source reads at `cb381593b255970ac63cd3a424ae91e68fa0020f`. No tests, builds, writes, or network calls were performed.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Missing path output suppresses the fallback

**Evidence:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:150–155` explicitly treats empty queue outputs as “run everything.” The existing fixture condition at lines 1124–1125 likewise skips only an explicit `artifact_only=true`. R3 instead requires an explicit `ovpr_paths=true` on PRs.

**Failure mode:** Checkout or an earlier step fails, or the new predicate fails before emitting its output. `ovpr_paths` is empty, so R3 skips Ubuntu even though the change set was never established as unrelated. R1’s fallback inside the predicate cannot cover a predicate that never runs.

**Disposition:** Change R3 to skip only an explicit negative result:

`always() && needs.changes.outputs.artifact_only != 'true' && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.changes.outputs.ovpr_paths != 'false')`

Emit `false` only after successful diff collection and matching. Extend R5 to cover missing output, failed diff, and unusable base, alongside the positive and negative path cases. The design cannot bind with R3 as written.

### 2. sharpens-framing — R2 omits direct runtime packaging inputs

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/release-e2e/packed-consumer.ts:94–114` packs and installs the launcher and runtime. `packages/runtime/scripts/stage-bundle.mjs:39–60` names core, types, and content as private runtime inputs; lines 112–124 copy types and core output; lines 135–147 execute `packages/content/stage-pack.mjs` and copy its result. None of `packages/content/**`, `packages/types/**`, or `packages/core/package.json` appears in R2.

**Failure mode:** A content-staging or private-package metadata change can break the packed installation while being classified as unrelated on the PR. This is a direct packaging omission, beyond the acknowledged possibility that arbitrary core code affects the fixture.

**Disposition:** Retain selective PR coverage, but add these direct packaging inputs and regression examples to R2/R5. Explicitly accept delayed feedback for other excluded core changes, covered by the unfiltered Ubuntu merge-group run.

The strongest alternative is filtering on all core changes: it avoids maintaining an incomplete dependency approximation. I reject that for this scope because it defeats the explicit scope-code skip criterion. Requiring complete lifecycle coverage before queue entry would change that judgment.

### 3. footnote — Preserve the existing predicate trust boundary

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:134–148` deliberately loads predicate code from the base tree so a PR cannot change its own classification through the script. Reuse that pattern for the new script, including “script absent → run fixture” on its first landing.

This is a limited protection: the PR workflow itself remains a separate control surface. Pass branch names through quoted environment variables, as the existing workflow does, rather than interpolating untrusted values into shell source.

### 4. footnote — Envelope ceiling differs from the single-seat contract

The envelope sets ceiling `7017515975`; the Stop 1 write-back is `7017511745`. The pinned contract’s “Envelope and ceiling” section specifies the write-back as the round-one ceiling for a single critic; its post-deposit exception applies to two or more critics.

I honored the explicit envelope ceiling. The intervening deposit supplies dispatch bookkeeping, not another critic’s verdict. This is a parent-side protocol discrepancy, not a product-design blocker.

Problem: the two OVPR lifecycle fixture jobs in `ci.yml` run on every pull request that is not artifact-only, each with a full install and build. The Windows leg is most of the cost.

- It does not filter on all of `packages/core`; core changes outside the list are covered on merge_group, not on the pull request.

metadata.issueBody:
The two advisory jobs #6698 added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `ovpr-fixture` (ubuntu, 12 min cap) and `ovpr-fixture-windows` (windows-latest, 15 min cap), run on every PR that is not artifact-only. Each does a full `pnpm install` and build. They are not in the merge gate's `needs`, but they add runner time to every PR, while #6584, #6585 and #6586 are removing CI cost.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On pull requests, the OVPR fixture jobs run only when the change set touches launcher, runtime, hook, deposit or install files (a path filter through the existing `changes` job outputs).
- [ ] The Windows fixture leg runs on pushes to master (or a schedule), not on every pull request, until the Phase 4 exit makes it required.
- [ ] A pull request that changes only unrelated files (for example docs or scope code) runs neither fixture job.
- [ ] A pull request that changes a launcher or hook file still runs the fixture job.

Refs #6698, #6614, #6621, #6586
